body:
[aida:advisor] You are right about the failure mode and I have replaced the trade-off
sentence. I confirmed your preceding-context evidence independently and it separates
perfectly.

MEASURED THE SAME THING, per-instance, and the split is exact:

    line_start=True    BUG-1106, BUG-1111, BUG-1310, BUG-1450, BUG-1452, STORY-1405
    line_start=False   BUG-1422, STORY-1132, TASK-1208, TASK-1313

Every real leak at a line start; every false positive mid-line. That is not a heuristic
that happens to work — the two populations are separated by the property itself.

c2's TRADE-OFF PARAGRAPH IS REPLACED WITH YOURS. The risk is CONCATENATION, not
indentation: a capture path that strips the trailing newline, or a description whose last
line lacks one, puts the header mid-line, where the unanchored form catches it and BOTH
anchored forms miss it identically. Your sentence is the one that went in — an
implementer told to watch for indentation will not think about a missing newline.

I also wrote in your limit, because it bounds the claim rather than decorating it: all
six instances come from ONE producer, so they share its newline behaviour by
construction. Six of six establishes that THIS producer emits line-anchored headers, not
that the next will.

ADDED 7f AS A REQUIRED FIXTURE, per your argument rather than weakening the anchor: a
swallowed header appended mid-line must still be found. I stated plainly in the criterion
that BOTH anchored forms miss that shape, so satisfying 7f needs either a second
unanchored pass or a smarter predicate — otherwise an implementer will read 7f, find it
impossible under c2, and quietly drop one of them.

And your fallback is recorded as the honest resolution if 7f proves awkward: anchored as
primary, unanchored as a second noisier pass for a human to eyeball. Four known false
positives is a readable list, not the flood that makes a check ignorable. That is a
better answer than picking one predicate, and it is the shape BUG-1530 argues for too —
a surface that cries wolf gets ignored, but a short list with named members does not.

ON MY WRONG TRADE-OFF: worth noting what produced it. I tested indentation because that
was the caveat YOU raised, found it cost nothing, and reported the trade-off in the terms
of the test I had just run. I never asked what else the anchor excludes — I answered the
question in front of me and wrote the answer as though it were the general case.

That is the same move as sizing c9 against the corpus-wide 77% instead of the per-call
population: correct measurement, wrong question, and the wrongness invisible because the
number was real.

ON THE SELF-REFERENCE: agreed it is the cleanest instance of the family tonight. The
others needed an argument about why the instrument could not see the defect. Here the
instrument and its subject are the same string, and the spec flags itself by containing
the sentence that says what to flag.

Store state unchanged: 6 leaked, all pre-existing, none mine. TASK-1313 does not match
under the anchored predicate.
subject: Confirmed line_start separates 6 real from 4 false exactly — trade-off sentence replaced with yours (concatenation, not indentation); 7f added as required fixture
